extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students and researchers interested in humor studies, ethnic relations, and cultural sociology
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and analyze what constitutes an ethnic joke, its typical themes and targets, theoretical accounts of how it works, and its social effects (acceptability, reinforcement of stereotypes, potential for harm or resistance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an ethnic joke
rubrics_metrics.description: An ethnic joke is a remark aiming at humor relating to an ethnic, racial or cultural group, often referring to an ethnic stereotype of the group in question for its punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the basic identifying feature: jokes that rely on ethnicity and stereotypical attributes to produce a punchline fall into this category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceptions and acceptability (ingroup vs outgroup)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perceptions of ethnic jokes are ambivalent; while many find them racist and offensive, for some people jokes poking fun at one's own ethnicity may be considered acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptability often depends on who tells the joke and who is the target (self-directed or in-group joking can be seen as permissible; out-group directed jokes are more likely to be judged racist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor mechanism: reliance on negative ethnic stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethnic jokes are often found funny exactly for the same reason they sound racist for others; it happens when they play on negative ethnic stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should note whether the joke's punchline depends on activating and exploiting a negative stereotype (the primary mechanism producing humor for some audiences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for harm and reinforcement of stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Davies maintains that ethnic jokes reinforce ethnic stereotypes and sometimes lead to calls for violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should consider the extent to which a joke consolidates harmful views about a group and whether it could contribute to hostility or real-world consequences (example: Polish jokes prompting diplomatic complaints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Common thematic content
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Davies, ethnic jokes are centered on the three main themes of stupidity, canniness and sexual behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing content, identify which of these theme(s) the joke uses, since these recur across traditions and shape the type of stereotype being invoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical targets and social positioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes in every country have certain targets for stupidity jokes – people who dwell on the edge of that nation or domain and who are perceived as culturally ambiguous by the dominant people of the center; they will likely be rustic people or immigrants in search of unskilled and low-prestige manual work. They are to a great extent similar to the joke-tellers themselves, share the same cultural background or even speak a similar or identical language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should note the social distance of the target (marginalized, immigrant, regional) and the relationship between teller and target (often similar but positioned as 'other' in some respect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical structure: Semantic Script Theory and binary oppositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Davies' approach is based on Victor Raskin's Semantic Script Theory of Humor, particularly arguments connected with ethnic humor on binary oppositions (e.g., stupid/clever).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses can examine which scripts or binary oppositions a joke exploits and how the script-switch produces the punchline; this helps explain why particular ethnic jokes work in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function as social resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethnic jokes can also be a form of social resistance, and so they are addressed by the joke-tellers against those whom they see as the aggressors (example: jokes published in Mexico about Americans).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the direction and intent of the joke: whether it targets dominant/aggressive groups as a way to resist or criticize, rather than merely denigrate a marginalized group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trajectory toward escalation (descent into violent depiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ethnic joke and the accompanying stereotype can undergo a descent as the target is depicted increasingly in terms of violent behaviour (example: the transformation of 'Paddy' in comic art into a degenerate bent on murder or outrage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether comedic depiction risks escalation into dehumanizing or violent portrayals, indicating a harmful evolution of the stereotype beyond mere ridicule.
